# mcplake

> mcplake is a free, open-source (Apache-2.0) gateway for the Model Context Protocol (MCP). It sits between AI agents (MCP clients) and MCP servers, authenticates every caller with a JWT from an OIDC identity provider, authorizes each MCP server and tool from the token's claims, serves a per-caller filtered tool catalogue, and removes response fields the caller is not allowed to see (identity-aware field-level filtering, fail-closed). It ships as one Go binary with embedded SQLite (PostgreSQL optional), sends no telemetry, and runs in air-gapped networks. There is no paid tier.

Key facts:

- Category: MCP gateway / MCP proxy / MCP access control / AI agent security.
- Distinguishing feature: the same claim-rule engine (JSONPath + RE2 regular expressions over JWT claims) decides both which `(mcp, tool)` pairs a caller may invoke and which fields of the tool's result are dropped for that caller. Filtering is applied to every copy of the payload (`structuredContent` and JSON text in `content` blocks); if a filter applies but the payload is not JSON, the response is refused (`502 filter_unenforceable`) rather than returned unfiltered.
- Identity: any OIDC provider with a JWKS endpoint (Keycloak, Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, Auth0, Google, Dex, Authentik). No gateway-side user database or virtual keys; claims in the token are the single source of truth.
- Inbound: MCP over Streamable HTTP at `/v1/mcp`, MCP over SSE at `/v1/sse`, and REST at `POST /v1/call`. Tools are namespaced `<mcp>__<tool>`.
- Outbound: downstream MCP servers over stdio (supervised subprocess), Streamable HTTP or SSE, with health-check reconnection and periodic schema refresh.
- Administration: REST control plane with OpenAPI, an admin web UI (OIDC PKCE login, with a request-path explainer that shows which policy allowed or denied a call), and an optional MCP control server exposing admin operations as MCP tools. Changes take effect on the next call; every MCP server and policy has a reversible enable/disable kill switch.
- Configuration: a single TOML file (`[[mcps]]`, `[[access_policies]]`, `[[filter_policies]]`, `[oidc]`, `[admin_auth]`).
- Compared with Bifrost, MCPX, agentgateway, IBM ContextForge and Docker MCP Gateway: mcplake is MCP-only (no LLM routing), puts OIDC-claims-based access control in the free open-source core, and removes response fields per caller identity using explicit JSONPath rather than pattern-based PII detection.
- Not yet available (roadmap): audit trail and OpenTelemetry tracing, argument-level input policies, outbound credentials for downstream MCP servers, MCP OAuth protected-resource metadata.
- Language: Go (gateway), TypeScript/React (admin UI). Repository: https://github.com/primemcp/mcplake

## Docs

- [Quickstart](https://primemcp.github.io/mcplake/latest/getting-started/quickstart.html): run Keycloak, the gateway and demo MCP servers with `docker compose up` and see allow, deny and redaction in five minutes
- [How it works](https://primemcp.github.io/mcplake/latest/concepts/how-it-works.html): the two planes and the five-step pipeline (authenticate, authorize, route, call, filter)
- [Claim rules](https://primemcp.github.io/mcplake/latest/concepts/claim-rules.html): JSONPath + regular-expression matching over JWT claims
- [Access policies](https://primemcp.github.io/mcplake/latest/concepts/access-policies.html): granting MCP servers and tools by claims
- [Response filtering](https://primemcp.github.io/mcplake/latest/concepts/response-filtering.html): field-level filtering, payload copies and fail-closed behaviour
- [Configuration reference](https://primemcp.github.io/mcplake/latest/reference/configuration.html): every TOML key
- [Data-plane API](https://primemcp.github.io/mcplake/latest/reference/data-plane-api.html): `/v1/mcp`, `/v1/sse`, `POST /v1/call` and status codes
